subject: music

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · Paper 1 Listening (written) · Component 2 Performing (coursework) · Component 3 Composing (coursework)

note: Units follow the Paper 1 Listening content: the syllabus's terminology for the musical elements first, then the seven areas of study in order, with areas of study 1–3 anchored on their focus works. The atlas program covers the examinable Listening strand; a closing atlas-only unit tracks the music-cognition lesson, which sits beyond the syllabus.

program.title: The elements of music
topics: Melody: melodic movement, arpeggio, countermelody, leitmotif, hook, riff, rāga
Scales and modes: major, minor, chromatic, modal, pentatonic, rāga, maqām
Rhythm and metre: simple and compound time, syncopation, hemiola, cross-rhythm, polyrhythm, tāla
Tempo: Italian markings, accelerando, rallentando, rubato, BPM
Tonality: major and minor, modulation to related keys
Harmony: primary and secondary chords, dominant seventh, cadences, consonance and dissonance, pedals
Texture: monophonic, homophonic, polyphonic, heterophonic, unison, antiphonal, drone
Musical devices: repetition, sequence, imitation, ostinato, Alberti bass
Dynamics: pianissimo to fortissimo, crescendo, diminuendo, terraced dynamics
Articulation and ornaments: legato, staccato, trill, mordent, appoggiatura, acciaccatura

program.title: Instruments, structure and notation
topics: Instruments, ensembles and voices: string quartet, SATB, pop and rock, orquesta tipica, Hindustani, silk and bamboo, takht
Instrumental and vocal techniques, and word-setting: pizzicato, glissando, tremolo, melisma, syllabic, rap, word-painting
Structure: binary, ternary, rondo, sonata form, minuet and trio, theme and variations, strophic, verse and chorus, call and response
Music technology and production: sample, loop, reverb, delay, overdubbing, multi-tracking, drum machine
Notation: staff notation, clefs, key signatures, note values, intervals, transposing instruments

program.section: Areas of study 1–3: the western classical tradition
program.title: Area of study 1: Baroque music
topics: Focus works: Vivaldi, Spring from The Four Seasons, movement 1 (Allegro)
Focus works: Handel, Concerto Grosso in D major Op. 6, No. 5 (HWV 323)
The solo concerto and the concerto grosso
Ripieno, concertino and basso continuo
Baroque performance practice and wider listening

program.section: Areas of study 1–3: the western classical tradition
program.title: Area of study 2: Classical music
topics: Focus work: Mozart, Quintet for piano and winds in E flat major, K. 452, movement 1
Chamber music for three to six players
Sonata form: exposition, development, recapitulation, first and second subject
Classical style and wider listening

program.section: Areas of study 1–3: the western classical tradition
program.title: Area of study 3: Romantic music
topics: Focus work: Smetana, Vltava from Ma Vlast
Single-movement works for orchestra
Programme music and the common trends of the Romantic era

program.section: Areas of study 4–7: music of cultures and contexts
program.title: Area of study 4: Music and words
topics: Art song for solo voice; music for choirs; popular song and songs from musicals
The ways composers set words to music and enhance the meaning of the text
Common structures and techniques found in modern song writing

program.section: Areas of study 4–7: music of cultures and contexts
program.title: Area of study 5: Music for dance
topics: Tango; Salsa; EDM (Electronic Dance Music)
African and western influences in the Latin American sound: habanera, marcado, clave
How music technology is used to create EDM: breakdown, build up, drop

program.section: Areas of study 4–7: music of cultures and contexts
program.title: Area of study 6: Music for small ensemble
topics: Silk and bamboo ensembles
Hindustani classical music: rāga, tāla, ālāp, jōr, gat, jhālā
Arab takht ensembles: maqām, īqā'āt
Identifying instruments, style-specific features and social and performance contexts

program.section: Areas of study 4–7: music of cultures and contexts
program.title: Area of study 7: Music for stage and screen
topics: Ballet music; film music; video game music
Orchestral music to accompany visual action
How musical features create atmosphere, increase tension and excitement and enhance moments of action

program.title: Why music moves us: atlas extension
topics: Music cognition: why brains find some patterns irresistible
